error_reason: The WebSurfer agent repeatedly performed search queries and scrolled to the top of search engine result pages without actually clicking on the search results to access the specific content (e.g., the actual Britannica or Tate pages). Consequently, the text visible in the viewport only consisted of the DuckDuckGo search interface ads and menus, failing to extract the required death date information despite the Planner's instructions to verify the date.

suggested_fix.fix_text: The agent stopped during search queries. Try clicking on the first search result link to visit the source page directly instead of just reading the search snippet.

probe_details.notes: The error analysis incorrectly labels the turns as 'incomplete_verification' due to the agent scrolling to the top. However, the TRACE CONTEXT explicitly shows that in Turn 11 and Turn 13, the agent successfully navigated to the actual URLs (Tate.org.uk and a Britannica search result page). The Planner's analysis in Turn 12 and 14 correctly identifies that the visible viewport did not contain the specific day (August 13), leading to the next query. The 'error' was actually a reasonable limitation of the browser simulation (viewport constraints) handled correctly by the Planner's logic to re-query, not a failure to click links. The analysis falsely accuses the agent of not clicking links when the logs prove it did click and load the specific artist pages.
